Responsibilities for kennel doors
New colleagues will find here how the first steps go

This page covers the daily responsibilities for kennel doors and why they matter to the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways. Good door checks protect animals, reassure travelers, and keep handoffs smooth from booking through pickup. When you work this desk, you are not just processing travel details. You are helping make sure each pet stays secure, calm, and accounted for while moving between skyports.

Start by treating every kennel as a live safety task. Before an animal is moved, confirm that the door is shut, latched, and free of damage. Look for bent edges, weak clips, loose hinges, or any sign that a door could open on its own. If you notice a problem, do not push ahead and hope for the best. Set the kennel aside, tell the senior coordinator, and make sure the issue is recorded in the desk log. A careful pause is better than a rushed mistake.

When working with travelers, use clear and simple language. Explain what you are checking and why the pet must stay inside the kennel until staff give the go-ahead. If a traveler seems worried, stay calm and steady. People often take their cues from your tone, so a quiet and confident approach helps the animal too. If a traveler like Anika Martin or Alina Tanaka asks for reassurance, keep your answer focused on the process and the welfare of the pet. If a pet like Trixie appears restless, do not open the door unless the right handoff step has been completed.

Keep the desk area orderly, because clutter makes mistakes more likely. Place paperwork where it will not be mixed with other files. Return kennel tags to the correct carrier. Check that each doorway and transfer point stays clear during movement. Small habits matter here, especially when several arrivals and pickups are happening around the same stretch of work.

If you are unsure, stop and ask. Never guess about a latch, a transfer, or a handoff. What to remember is simple: secure doors, careful checks, and calm communication protect every animal and every traveler.
